PullRequest.Title: Agents mode: edit only User settings in the mode
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #350716 (stacked on it): in Agents mode, the Settings editor edits only User settings.

**Landing order:** #350716, then this PR, then the PR that adds the Agents mode toggle. #350716 alone has no way to turn the mode on, so the crash below can't happen yet. The toggle makes the mode reachable, so it depends on this PR.

## Why this is needed

Agents mode switches an editor window to the Agents workspace without reloading. That workspace has no settings of its own. The window says it has a workspace open, but there is no workspace file and no folder behind it, and the mode refuses workspace writes ("Workspace Settings are not available in this window").

Without this PR, in a window in the mode:
- **Opening Workspace Settings crashes.** The lookup for the workspace settings file falls back to the first folder of the workspace, and there is none, so it throws instead of opening anything.
- **Entering the mode hits the same crash.** When the window's workspace state changes, the Settings menu updates itself, which calls the same lookup.
- **The Settings editor still offers the Workspace and Folder tabs.** A change made there fails, because the mode can't write workspace settings.

The mode reads User and application settings, so User settings are the only place where an edit takes effect.

## What changes

- `PreferencesService.workspaceSettingsResource` returns nothing when the workspace has neither a workspace file nor folders, instead of throwing. The Settings menu update adds its workspace-settings item only when there is a workspace settings file.
- `SettingsTargetsWidget` changes in the mode:
  - The Workspace and Folder targets are disabled.
  - A Workspace or Folder target becomes User, whether it was chosen, restored from the editor's saved state or asked for by a link.
  - Leaving the mode enables them again.
- `SettingsEditor2` tells the widget when the mode changes.
- `PreferencesService`: Open Workspace Settings and Open Folder Settings open User settings in the mode.

## How to test

1. Set `"chat.agentsMode.enabled": true`, reload, and turn the mode on (`IAgentsModeService.setActive(true)` until the toggle lands). Nothing throws while entering.
2. In the Settings editor, the Workspace and Folder tabs are disabled and the User tab is selected. This holds even when the editor was on the Workspace tab before.
3. Run Preferences: Open Workspace Settings (JSON): User settings open.
4. Turn the mode off: the Workspace tab is available again.

Unit tests:
- `settingsEditor2.test.ts`:
  - The folder target of a multi-root workspace moves to User on entering.
  - Workspace or folder targets asked for in the mode stay User.
- `preferencesService.test.ts`:
  - Workspace and folder settings open User settings in the mode.
  - A workspace with neither a workspace file nor folders has no workspace settings. This test throws without the fix.

## Validation

On 5d9ffc0c99f:
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <file>`, all passed:
  - `preferencesService.test.ts`: 10
  - `settingsEditor2.test.ts`: 26
  - `settingsTreeModels.test.ts`: 81
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check` and `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed.

## Known limits

- The redirect is per entry point. Longer term, the Agents workspace should report no editable workspace or folder settings resource, so every caller gets it right.

Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @sandy081

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The folder-target normalization and synchronous event chain directly establish two uncoalesced calls with the same final view state; the complete model recreation is traced. Additional configuration events can cause more work, but are not needed for this finding. Duration depends on catalog size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Settings model objects, layout-resolution CPU, forced tree renders, and grouped installed-extension requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Two full O(S) model reconstructions per affected mode entry, where S includes core and extension-contributed settings; two list requests per enabled extension-management server, not per installed extension. Backend scanner coalescing can share the scan but does not merge the renderer rebuilds.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Duplicate UI refresh work, CPU/GC pressure and jank during mode entry
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An ordinary target-change notification caused one full rebuild through onDidSettingsTargetChange. There was no mode listener issuing another unconditional rebuild after that same target-change notification.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added mode handler invokes a target-normalizing setter that can already trigger a full rebuild, then unconditionally invokes a second full rebuild.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added settingsEditor2.ts:968-970 sets the mode, calls setAgentsMode, then calls onConfigUpdate unconditionally; added preferencesWidgets.ts:356-357 routes the existing folder target through updateTarget, whose existing event fires the first rebuild.
Findings.Title: Coalesce the target change and mode refresh into one rebuild
Findings.Impact: Entering Agents mode while the Settings editor is on a folder target in a multi-root window performs two complete Settings model rebuilds and renders for the same final state. Large extension-contributed Settings catalogs incur duplicate renderer CPU/allocation and visible refresh jank. When extension recommendations are enabled, both invocations also request the installed-extension list.
Findings.Evidence: onDidChangeAgentsMode sets viewState.isAgentsMode, then calls settingsTargetsWidget.setAgentsMode. For a selected folder target, setAgentsMode -> updateTarget -> _onDidTargetChange.fire synchronously invokes onDidSettingsTargetChange, which already calls onConfigUpdate(undefined, true) at line 960. The added line 970 immediately starts another identical refresh. onConfigUpdate has no in-flight joining: each invocation resolves the full layout, awaits extension data, refreshes models and forces rendering. SettingsTreeModel.update (settingsTreeModels.ts:638-651, 697-753) recreates all group/setting elements and disposes the previous children.
Findings.Recommendation: Update the mode and normalized target atomically and request one refresh, or coalesce these same-turn full refresh requests. Keep an explicit mode refresh when normalization does not emit a target change.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added loop, startup await, fresh configuration caches, and full-tree cloning implementation are directly traced. Unchanged defaults exhaust the folder loop even for empty folder configurations. Exact pause duration and the prevalence of very large multi-root windows are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread configuration lookups/deep comparisons and complete merged configuration-tree allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For S mostly unchanged registered keys and F distinct folders, up to 2*S*(F+1) getValue calls plus one full merged-tree clone per folder on each folder-bearing side, with additional per-language comparisons. Cache reuse bounds clones within one switch, but fresh parsed snapshots repeat them on the next switch.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Longer synchronous mode switches and restored-window startup, with transient allocation and GC pressure proportional to folder count times configuration-tree size
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The base desktop window used WorkspaceService directly and had no mode-switch snapshot comparison. Its consolidated folder models were lazy and reused for actual resource consumers; it did not create fresh copies of every folder's merged configuration for this operation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new mode-switch path reconstructs snapshot caches and eagerly queries the full registered-setting union at every folder before announcing configuration changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 269-277 create fresh BaseConfiguration snapshots, union their allKeys(), expand overrides to all folders, and invoke getValue on both configurations inside the key-by-folder loop; switchDelegates calls this synchronously, and desktop.main.ts:340-341 awaits restoration.
Findings.Title: Limit switch comparisons to changed layers and folder overrides
Findings.Impact: Entering or leaving Agents mode in a multi-root window with tens or hundreds of folders synchronously evaluates thousands of registered settings across those folders and eagerly clones complete configuration trees for folders without open editors. This increases mode-switch latency and renderer CPU/GC pressure; restored mode also awaits this work before workspace-trust initialization.
Findings.Evidence: fireConfigurationSwitch parses both snapshots into fresh BaseConfiguration instances, takes allKeys(), and checks each unchanged key against every folder. BaseConfiguration.getFolderConsolidatedConfiguration (configurationModels.ts:1126-1138) caches one workspaceConfiguration.merge(folderConfiguration) per folder; ConfigurationModel.merge (same file:157-159) deep-clones the complete contents and overrides, even when the folder configuration is empty. Those caches are new for every switch, so existing delegate caches cannot serve the comparisons.
Findings.Recommendation: Derive candidates from differences in the configuration layers and configured folder/ language-override keys, and restrict folder-specific comparisons to affected keys/folders instead of evaluating every default against every folder. Preserve the resource- and language-aware ConfigurationChangeEvent semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a desktop editor window and restore or toggle Agents mode, including a multi-root window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing configuration, storage and keyboard-layout initialization run in parallel. A persisted active mode then awaits setAgentsMode before workspace-trust construction. Explicit toggles await delegate initialization and the synchronous configuration comparison before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load profile settings and, for a separate non-default settings profile, default-profile application settings; register their watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional profile settings read per mode entry, plus one application settings read when applicable. The newly entered Agents workspace has no workspace file or folders, so no folder settings reads occur at entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Desktop startup initialized the editor WorkspaceService only; these additional Agents configuration reads and watchers did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited during delegate creation and therefore on startup restoration and explicit entry paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read cached configuration-default overrides if the localStorage existence marker is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one extra cache-file read per newly created Agents configuration. ConfigurationCache retains cache-file handles, not file contents; each new delegate can read again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the editor configuration initialized its defaults cache on this startup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes policy and user configuration initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously compare configuration snapshots across registered keys, folder resources and language overrides, warming fresh merged configuration trees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Mostly unchanged keys require comparisons across F distinct folders; each snapshot cache builds at most one complete merged tree per applicable folder, not one clone per key. Work repeats with fresh snapshots on every switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No mode-switch comparison existed; actual resource consumers reused the editor's lazy consolidated caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks switch completion and, during restoration, subsequent startup initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Thousands of core/extension settings, tens or hundreds of folders in large multi-root windows, configured language identifiers, and repeated mode entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One switchQueue serializes entries, exits and active-profile recreation. Profile/application loading is parallel after defaults initialization; configuration comparison executes synchronously on the renderer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mode delegates are lazy until entry and disposed on exit. Their settings models are recreated on reentry. Snapshot consolidation and language caches coalesce work within one comparison but start cold again on each switch, independently of warm delegate caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startup await, fresh snapshot caches, per-folder full-tree merging and key/folder loop are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No durations or heap measurements were collected. Large multi-root prevalence is uncertain; the mode UI toggle is outside this diff, while the setter and persisted restoration path are implemented here.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the eager all-key/all-folder comparison. The bounded extra configuration reads and managed watcher ownership do not independently warrant findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enter Agents mode with the Settings editor showing a multi-root folder target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The mode event updates view state and normalizes the target. Settings refreshes are not awaited by the switch, but their synchronous layout work and eventual full model reconstruction/rendering run on the renderer and determine when the updated editor is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request installed-extension metadata when experimental recommendation data is enabled and applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two logical list refreshes for the duplicate full rebuilds; each is grouped by extension-management server, not by extension. Supported local mode has no remote extension server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An ordinary target change initiated one rebuild and one grouped list refresh under the same recommendation condition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each Settings rebuild awaits its request before reconstructing/rendering the model; the mode setter itself does not await these requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan installed extensions to service list requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Concurrent requests for the same profile/language share scanAllExtensionPromise; two IPC requests therefore need not cause two underlying scans. Each caller still converts and returns its extension list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scanner and in-flight sharing served the prior single target-change list request; the diff increases request count, not the per-extension scan design.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the awaited list request, not the mode setter's awaited critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch recommended extension gallery metadata on cache miss, and manifests for missing recommendation groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Successful toggle data is cached window-wide, so warm rebuilds issue no gallery metadata requests. Cold or failed-cache concurrent rebuilds may each query the recommendation list, sequentially within each rebuild; manifests are only requested for absent groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same recommendation helper and network operations existed on full refresh; the new handler can invoke them twice rather than once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before model rendering, with existing timeouts; off the mode setter's awaited path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total Settings catalog size, including extension-contributed settings, installed extension count, and applicable recommendation count; duplicate rebuild multiplicity is two, independent of folder count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Target-change notification is synchronous and starts the first refresh before the handler starts the second. Their asynchronous phases overlap; both subsequently recreate models and force rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No in-flight coalescing exists for onConfigUpdate. Successful recommendation metadata is cached, absent/failure results are not; backend extension scans have same-profile/language in-flight sharing. Neither cache merges the two full renderer model rebuilds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: folder-target normalization, synchronous event delivery, two calls and recursive full model recreation are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact jank depends on catalog size and recommendation settings. Warm network caches limit external requests but do not eliminate duplicate renderer allocation and rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported duplicate full rebuilds caused by the unconditional mode refresh after target normalization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and edit User, Workspace or Folder Settings while in Agents mode; display read-only settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace/folder entry points redirect to the existing User Settings opening path. JSON opening awaits settings-file creation checks and editor resolution; graphical opening uses a cached editor input and the existing asynchronous Settings rendering path. Writes use the existing editing queue and reload configuration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected settings file and create it only if missing before JSON editor opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected User settings resource per request; a missing resource adds one write. Text-model resolution can reuse an already-open model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Settings JSON entry points already used these creation/read helpers for their selected target; the redirect selects User rather than workspace/folder and removes workspace-specific preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, parse, edit and write one settings JSON file; application/all-profile keys can select the default profile resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read and one write per queued settings-file update; application routing changes the file selected, not the number of files edited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Agents configuration editing helper already performed this single-file read/edit/write operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Writes are serialized and awaited by the existing update operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Settings-file bytes, configured properties, currently visible Settings rows, and frequency of user edits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing configuration-editing Queue serializes writes. Existing 50 ms configuration reload schedulers and 100 ms folder-change debounce remain in place.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Settings input/default models and open text models are reused. Read-only metadata does not introduce a new renderer or serialization pipeline. Checkbox/list disposables remain registered before the new early return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in redirect routing, single-file operations and unchanged widget disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Settings-file size and file-provider latency were not measured; no increased boundary cardinality is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression: target/read-only changes alter behavior or select existing resources without independently increasing expensive work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change the active user profile while Agents mode has mounted folders
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Profile-change participants join profile completion. The wrapper queues recreation of its Agents configuration, loads the new profile/application settings and existing mounted folder configurations, switches delegates and compares snapshots. The Agents workspace itself survives.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recreate profile-dependent configuration and load settings/tasks/launch/MCP files for mounted folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile settings read, optional application settings read and defaults cache read; four configuration resource reads per distinct mounted folder. Folder loads are sequential, with each folder's four reads parallel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no desktop Agents-mode delegate to recreate. Normal editor profile handling existed separately; the Agents window's existing loader already loaded four files per mounted folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Joined to profile completion before the new delegate is announced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct mounted session folders, four configuration resources each, settings bytes and registered settings/language overrides.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: switchQueue serializes delegate replacement with mode switches. User/application reads are parallel; mounted folders are loaded sequentially. Snapshot comparison is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace identity/folders survive, but the old configuration is disposed on replacement, including watchers; folder configuration caches are recreated rather than retained. Existing editor profile handling continues on its retained delegate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in joined profile recreation, four resources per folder and disposal; comparison cost is the same reported root cause as mode switching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical mounted-session folder count is uncertain and no file-load duration was measured. More folders amplify recreation cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: The snapshot-comparison finding also applies here. No separate claim that required profile configuration recreation or pre-existing serial folder loading is itself a new actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mount, remove or move a session folder to an alternate worktree in Agents mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Alternate moves resolve the destination, settle local trust, then enter the folder-update queue. Folder will-change participants load destination configuration before workspace update and did-change notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the primary folder's real path for alternate-location matching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one realpath read per primary-folder resolution on a cache miss. Mounted primaries retain successful forms/in-flight promises; a primary not currently mounted is not retained and can be read again on later moves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing ordinary single-folder move used the same provider resolution and realpath helper; the diff extends that route to mounted folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before validating and applying the move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List agent-host sessions when required to resolve a worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared host-wide list request per invalid cache refresh, not per candidate worktree or mounted folder. Warm valid cache issues no list request; refreshes join the store's in-flight promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary folder-location resolution used the same session-list store and cache/coalescing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold unresolved worktree matching can await the list before proceeding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the added destination folder's settings, tasks, launch and MCP configuration and watch those resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four file reads per added distinct folder; a move adds exactly one destination and removes one source. Batch additions process folders sequentially, each with parallel resource reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents folder additions already used this configuration loader. The new move reuses an add/remove event rather than adding a per-setting or per-worktree boundary fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Joined to will-change processing before updating the mounted folder.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Added/moved mounted folders, session-list size and provider count. A single move concerns one folder, not every repository or every alternate worktree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers resolve sequentially until one succeeds. Folder edits share a Queue and await all will-change joiners. Trust lookups for local file URIs use local trust state, not remote canonicalization; four destination resource reads are parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session listing is positive-cache/in-flight shared; unknown locations can cause a refresh but a valid list prevents another host call. Removed folder configurations/watchers are disposed; primary-location entries transfer on move and are deleted on removal. Pending folder changes use WeakMap.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in grouped session listing, one-folder move cardinality and queue/disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-list size, provider latency and mount counts are unknown; no boundary count increase beyond the newly supported operation is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent regression: new moves reuse bounded existing loading and coalesced location resolution. Primary-location pending APIs have no production callers in this snapshot, so speculative unbounded retention was omitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new native workspace from Agents mode, including declined or failed entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Stop extension hosts, leave Agents mode, resolve/initialize the destination workspace, request main-process entry and migrate storage. If entry is declined or fails before completion, restore the prior mode before restarting hosts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop existing extension-host processes and restart them on the existing entry/recovery paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stop/restart cycle per attempted workspace entry, grouped by extension host rather than extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native workspace entry already stopped hosts and restarted them on its existing completion/recovery paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stop precedes entry; host restart precedes recovered extension availability. Newly added mode exit/restore occurs while hosts are stopped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve workspace identity, request workspace entry and switch workspace storage through existing platform services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination workspace per attempt, with one entry request and one storage switch only after successful entry; no per-folder entry calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native entry and successful storage migration operations existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited as part of entering the workspace; refusal gates restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize destination editor configuration and, on unsuccessful entry, recreate the prior Agents configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing destination workspace configuration loading remains grouped by destination resources; refusal/error adds one Agents delegate recreation with profile/application reads and no restored mounted folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no Agents mode to exit or recreate on this native entry path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mode exit precedes destination initialization; failure restoration is awaited before host recovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Destination folders/configuration size, extension-host count, and frequency of unsuccessful entry attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entry workflow is ordered; mode changes use switchQueue. Extension hosts stop in reverse order, and existing startup waits for local-process host readiness. No new per-folder subprocess burst was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mode exit disposes Agents delegates; failed entry restoration creates fresh ones. Successful destination entry does not restore the old mode, and storage migration remains success-only.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in ordering and before/after boundary cardinalities; no unnecessary extra host restart or storage migration was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User-declined/failed entry frequency and delegate recreation latency are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression beyond the reported configuration comparison on mode exit/restore. Required recovery and existing entry boundaries were not treated as generic optimization findings.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 32 changed files and every diff page against e6d424c4bce7a07a1133cc530c4570df8dad3558, with a distinct performance pass and surrounding call-path/cache/lifecycle analysis. Submitted two introduced regressions: eager all-key/all-folder snapshot comparison and duplicate Settings rebuilds. No qualifying performance-regression fix provenance was identified. Analysis is static; no scripts, builds or modifications were performed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
